findings.title: Blocked-email match counters can be incremented multiple times for one signup attempt
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? is called from EmailValidator during User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save runs validations again. Each call executes record.match_count += 1 and record.save, so a single rejected account creation can increment match_count more than once and persists the increment even though no user is created. This corrupts the blocklist statistics and adds unnecessary writes.

findings.title: Match count update is not atomic and save failures are ignored
findings.body: should_block? loads a BlockedEmail row, increments match_count in Ruby, and saves it. Concurrent attempts with the same blocked email can read the same match_count and overwrite each other's increments. The return value of record.save is also ignored, so a failed update still leaves the method to decide blocking based on stale in-memory data. Use an atomic counter update if accurate statistics are needed.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is exact and unnormalized, so blocks can be bypassed by case or whitespace
findings.body: should_block? queries BlockedEmail.where(email: email) using the raw value. Neither this model nor the changed User validations normalize the address by stripping and downcasing it. A block entry for user@example.com will not match USER@EXAMPLE.COM or an address with surrounding whitespace, allowing a blocked user to register by changing case or whitespace. Normalize emails before storing and querying blocked entries.

findings.title: Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is not anchored and can match unintended domains
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds a regex of the form @(domains) with only dots escaped and matches it anywhere in the address. With a whitelist of example.com, user@example.com.attacker.com matches because it contains @example.com as a substring, so the whitelist can be bypassed. With a blacklist it can produce false positives for domains that merely contain a blocked domain as a prefix. Compare the actual domain or anchor the regex to the end of the address and escape each domain.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is defined as a shared mutable array on the controller prototype
findings.body: rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is placed directly on the Ember object prototype. Arrays defined this way are shared by all instances of the controller unless reinitialized in init. If the controller is instantiated more than once, including in tests, rejected email addresses leak between instances and persist unexpectedly. Initialize the array in init or reset it when the create-account modal is opened.
